dedupe_keys.name: fridge fast reactor input deck generator

description: FRIDGe is a software tool for generating input decks for fast-reactor simulations. The JOSS paper describes its use with liquid-metal fast-reactor configurations, where repeated manual setup of geometry, materials and operating assumptions can be error prone. A user supplies a reactor design and simulation settings, so the modelled facility, spatial detail and operating period are chosen for each run; FRIDGe does not contain a deployed reactor dataset. The public repository, examples and metadata are MIT licensed. Generated decks can support comparisons of nuclear-system design or safety cases by keeping inputs consistent across scenarios. A caveat is that an automatically generated file still needs checking against the solver specification and an independently justified physical model. The code does not itself license or run a reactor. No directly related catalogue record was established. The JOSS summary and own repository were read without generating a deck or running a nuclear solver.
